calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Penguins are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Penguins.

calls.body: It’s the Penguins’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Stars get more of the play than usual.

calls.head: Quality over quantity for the Stars
calls.body: When the Stars shoot, it’s usually a real chance, and the Penguins are one of the league’s worst at stopping that. The Penguins’ goalie is going to be busy in all the wrong ways.
calls.call: The Stars’ average shot has at least their usual 6.8% chance of going in.

DAL.head: We leaned Dallas’s way (57%), but Pittsburgh had other ideas.

surprises.head: Dallas couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Dallas usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Pittsburgh usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Dallas’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.8% (about 7.0% against Pittsburgh) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.
surprises.flipped: Quality over quantity for the Stars

story.head: Rakell wins it in a shootout
paras: Pittsburgh had a goal taken off because play should have been stopped earlier late in the first. Connor Dewar opened the scoring for the Penguins early in the third. Tyler Seguin tied it on the power play with 30 seconds left. It didn’t matter in the end. Ben Kindel, Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell scored in the shootout for the Pens, and Rakell’s in the fourth round ended it.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Artūrs Šilovs made 24 saves for the Penguins, and Jake Oettinger stopped 20 of 21. The Penguins moved to 3-2-1, and the Stars dropped to 2-2-1.

items.text: The Penguins won for the first time in four games.
Jamie Benn’s point streak against Pittsburgh ended after at least five games.
Tyler Seguin scored his first goal of the season, his first since Nov 15, 2025 (twelve games played since).
None of the preview’s three calls held.
